stem: Two rooms have the same relative humidity but different air temperatures. Why should their atmospheric drying demand not be assumed identical?
choices: Saturation vapor pressure changes with temperature, so the same relative humidity can correspond to different vapor pressure deficits
Relative humidity represents the fraction of saturation at each temperature, so matching RH makes the absolute vapor pressure equal in both rooms
Air temperature changes sensible heat load, but atmospheric vapor demand is determined by relative humidity without temperature input
Matching relative humidity indicates equal moisture content in the air, so differences in room temperature mainly affect equipment load
rationale: VPD is derived from the relationship between saturation vapor pressure and actual vapor pressure, so temperature and relative humidity must be interpreted together.
